subject: Nyx Systems — Acceptance evidence exchange: latency & throughput targets
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nyxsys.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Nyx Systems — Acceptance evidence exchange: latency & throughput targets

Hi Evan,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a first-pass targets spreadsheet that maps Nyx's concurrency and percentiles to Redwood's recommended test configurations (bucketed by session length and model selection). Key asks from our side to make the acceptance run actionable: 

- Confirm the three traffic profiles you want us to validate (we called them steady: 50 qps; ramp: 0->200 qps over 30 mins; burst: 600 qps for 5 mins).
- Provide a short sample of production request/response sizes (JSON or CSV) so we can tune KV caching and batching knobs.
- Let us know any strict latency SLOs below P95 that we must avoid (for example: P95 < 150ms for 8k-context sessions).

I attached: nyx_latency_throughput_targets_v1.xlsx (targets + mapping). We propose running the first acceptance stage next Wednesday (2027-06-16) morning Pacific for the steady + ramp profiles, and a burst window in the evening to avoid interfering with your dev deploys. Monica will run the harness and Dev will coordinate kernel/quantization choices on the host side.

If that schedule looks good I'll send a refined plan and a test run checklist.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: nyx_latency_throughput_targets_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nyxsys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@nyxsys.com>, Maya Chen <mchen@nyxsys.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nyx Systems — Acceptance evidence exchange: latency & throughput targets

Thanks Karthik — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from the Nyx side: 

1) Profiles: please add a 30-minute mixed-profile window (60% reads, 40% generative) that mimics our typical web tier.
2) Payload samples: attached three representative requests from our gateway (they're small, ~1.2KB typical).
3) SLOs: our internal goal is P95 < 180ms for short sessions (<2k tokens) and P95 < 350ms for long sessions (<=8k tokens). If you can flag significant regression at P50 as well that would be helpful.

We are fine with the 2027-06-16 morning run; evening burst is preferred after 20:00 PT. Maya from SRE will be on standby to validate host-level telemetry and confirm there's no interference with infra autoscaling.

On our side, please share the detailed step-by-step runbook so our SREs can follow along.

Thanks,
Evan
Head of Platform
Nyx Systems

Attachment: nyx_gateway_sample_requests.zip (3 JSON files, stubbed)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-06-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nyx Systems — Acceptance evidence exchange: latency & throughput targets

Evan — thanks, attached is the refined runbook and the technical checklist we'll execute during the window. Highlights: 

- Test harness: Redwood's continuous-batcher with prefix caching enabled for long sessions.
- Metrics captured: P50/P95/P99 per model variant, tail latencies (99.9), CPU/GPU utilization, kernel swap counts, and per-request token footprint.
- Validation gates: Pass requires no P95 regression >20% vs baseline for steady profile, and peak success rate >99% during burst for routing fallback.
- Timeboxed rollback: automatic fallback to a compatible model-quantization combo if P99 > 2s for more than 2 minutes.

Proposed schedule (PT):
- 08:30 — pre-run checklist & telemetry sanity (10m)
- 08:45 — steady profile (45m)
- 09:40 — ramp profile (30m)
- 10:15 — pause / data sync (15m)
- 20:00 — burst window (5 mins) + 20:10 — evening cooldown / traces pull

Attachments: nyx_load_test_plan_v2.xlsx, nyx_kpis_and_notes.docx (both included in Drive link). Monica will run the harness and push compiled traces to the shared Drive folder noted below.

Please confirm SRE contact and whether we should route traces to your internal S3 or to our encrypted transfer.

Regards,
Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nyxsys.com>, SRE Team <sre@nyxsys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-06-16T18:22:00-07:00
Subject: Nyx Systems — Run 1 results (steady + ramp) and artifacts

Evan / team,

We completed the steady and ramp profiles this morning. Attached are the summarized CSV and raw traces. High-level summary: 

- Steady (50 qps): P50=38ms, P95=162ms, P99=285ms. Pass vs Nyx short-session SLO (P95 < 180ms).
- Ramp (0->200 qps in 30m): P50=45ms, P95=198ms, P99=360ms. Slight exceed on P95 for ramp (10% over Nyx long-session SLO of 180ms) driven by a small subset of long-sequence requests.
- Observed tail events correlated with a particular quantized kernel path on 2 of 8 GPUs; Dev has flagged that kernel for a follow-up micro-benchmark and temporary routing change.

Attachments uploaded: nyx_run_20270616_results.csv, nyx_raw_traces_20270616.zip (full traces + per-host telemetry). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bNyxOnboardDocs

Next steps we propose:
1) Dev to run targeted micro-bench on the kernel path and attempt a patched kernel flip to reduce P99.
2) Rerun a short mixed-profile (30m) tomorrow evening during your low-traffic window to validate the fix under burst conditions.
3) We'll export a formal acceptance report once the burst window completes and all tails are <20% above baseline.

Quoted for context:

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nyxsys.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@nyxsys.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-06-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nyx Systems — Run 1 results (steady + ramp) and artifacts

Monica / Karthik — really appreciate the quick turnaround and clear artifacts. The team reviewed the CSV and traces: the ramp tail appears consistent with the kernel path you identified. Nyx SRE will accept the planned micro-bench + a follow-up short mixed-profile run tomorrow 20:15 PT. If the evening run reduces the P99 tail to within 20% of baseline, Nyx is prepared to sign off on the acceptance criteria and move to contract finalization.

Two small asks before the evening run: 
- Please provide a short single-page evidence note that maps the run artifacts to the acceptance gates (we can attach it to our procurement packet).
- Please add the exact command-lines you executed for the harness and the kernel flip so our SREs can reproduce the step.

We will get the DocuSign routing ready and target 2027-06-21 for final signatures, pending the evening run.

Thanks,
Evan
